claims.explanation: Vincristine kills cells by binding tubulin and causing mitotic arrest, and the decision between survival and death during arrest is governed by the balance of anti-apoptotic MCL1 and its degradation machinery. Selectivity is therefore expected to track with features that lower the apoptotic threshold (FBXW7 loss, low MCL1, high BCL2L11/BIM, TP53 pathway defects) and with features that reduce effective intracellular drug (high ABCB1/MRP efflux, low tubulin/target expression). The observed pattern is consistent with this: sensitive lines are enriched for TP53 and FBXW7 mutations and for BRAF/PTEN/RAS-driven contexts, while resistant lines include several with intact apoptotic signaling or efflux capacity.

features.basis: FBXW7 loss stabilizes MCL1 and impairs its mitotic degradation, lowering apoptotic threshold to antitubulins (PMID 21368834)
MCL1 is the key anti-apoptotic regulator of antitubulin-induced death; high MCL1 protects (PMID 21368834)
TP53 loss is enriched in the most killed lines and impairs mitotic checkpoint/apoptotic responses to spindle poisons
P-glycoprotein efflux reduces intracellular vincristine and confers resistance (PMID 7214365)
MRP1 overexpression confers moderate resistance to vincristine (PMID 7954421)
BIM is the BH3-only effector released during mitotic arrest that triggers apoptosis; high BIM sensitizes
Higher tubulin target levels can buffer drug binding and reduce mitotic arrest
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines (IGR37, WM793, 8305C, HEC265) are among the most killed
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines and may lower survival signaling
KRAS-mutant lines (NCIH1792, PATU8988T, RKN) are enriched among sensitive lines
CDKN2A loss is common in sensitive lines and may impair cell-cycle checkpoint control
SARM1 NADase mediates vincristine-induced axonal degeneration; in cancer cells it may modulate NAD+ and survival
